Manufacturing projects

Wire Cutter Fixture/Laser Cleaner

Increase the production of wire cutters going through laser cleaning

Goal

  • Design a fixture that securely holds product during the laser cleaning process
  • Alter the existing program to reduce cycle time
  • Fit within an 8″ × 8″ × 8″ frame
  • Withstand long exposure to a high-definition laser

Approach

  • Designed a base from 6061-T6 aluminum in Catia V5
  • Printed a test prototype on a Prusa Core One+
  • Designed for easy assembly with press-fit dowel pins
  • Adjusted the Z height and the laser shape and power code on the Trumpf laser marker

Results

  • Cycle time fell from 3:30 to 1:15, about 2.8× faster
  • Wire cutters cleaned per cycle rose from 4 to 5
  • Daily production of wire cutter pliers doubled, from 150 to 300
Software
Catia V5
Materials and processes
6061-T6 aluminum, 3D-printed test prototype, press-fit dowel pins
Status
Complete

Pneumatic Emboss Ball/Spring Loader Mechanism

Semi-automates and speeds up assembly of universal joint socket adapters

Goal

  • Design a mechanism that cuts assembly time by loading emboss balls and springs automatically and at the same time
  • Fit on a small desk
  • Make the device easy to assemble and manufacture

Approach

  • Researched pneumatic loading and timing mechanisms to see what applied to the design
  • Modeled the initial prototype in Catia V5 and 3D printed the assembly
  • Installed heat-set inserts so the prototype is modular

Results

  • Assembly time fell from 10 s to 2 s, 5× faster
  • The initial prototype was bulky and inconsistent
  • A new prototype is in development that simplifies the timing system, improves ergonomics, and is easier to assemble
Software
Catia V5
Materials and processes
3D printing, heat-set inserts, pneumatics
Status
Second prototype in development

Induction Heating Cell

Automates the hardening process for all plier families

Goal

  • The current cell is operated manually, which limits it to a standard 8-hour workday minus breaks
  • Design a new automated cell that can run during breaks and without constant operator supervision

Approach

  • Analyzed the current induction heating cell to understand how it works and where it could improve
  • Researched induction heating techniques, adjustable conveyors, and cooling technology
  • Designed the core frame in Catia V5 from AngleLock 8020 aluminum

Results

  • Core components are in place, and the initial prototype is still being designed
  • Components are being quoted for pricing
  • A bill of materials is being built to show what needs to be purchased
Software
Catia V5
Materials and processes
AngleLock 8020 aluminum frame, induction heating, adjustable conveyor
Status
In design, bill of materials in progress

Joint Bit Socket Fixture

Allows a new joint bit socket to be laser welded

Goal

  • Current fixtures hold sockets by a male connection, but a new socket needs a female connection
  • Design a new fixture that holds the new socket by its female connection
  • Withstand a high-definition laser

Approach

  • Called out the hexagonal cut of the female connection with GD&T
  • Modeled the female connection and the rest of the fixture in Catia V5 in 6061 aluminum with a black oxide finish
  • 3D printed multiple prototypes to confirm a secure hold
  • Simplified each new prototype to design for manufacturability

Results

  • Upper management approved the final design for production
  • A fixture pallet quote was requested from Bosch Rexroth
  • The machine shop manufactured the fixture, and it is now in use on the laser welder for mass production
Software
Catia V5, GD&T
Materials and processes
6061 aluminum, black oxide plating, 3D-printed prototypes
Status
In use for mass production

Formula Hybrid racecar

FSAE Firewall

Protects the driver from dangerous temperatures from the engine and high-voltage components

Goal

  • Make the firewall lighter while still protecting the driver from dangerous temperatures
  • Add a cutout for the wiring harness that complies with the FSAE rulebook

Approach

  • Changed the material from stainless steel to 6061 aluminum and the attachment from welding to rivets and nuts, using decision matrices
  • Used SolidWorks sheet metal to turn a panel assembly into one piece, and outsourced production to Evology
  • Shaped the cutouts from sheet metal on a brake press

Results

  • Firewall weight fell by 20 lb while still passing every test needed for rules compliance
  • The car won 2nd place at the 2025 Formula Hybrid Competition
Software
SolidWorks (sheet metal)
Materials and processes
6061 aluminum, rivets and nuts, brake press, production by Evology
Status
Passed rules compliance

Nose Cone

Reworks the nose cone so it complies with FSAE rules

Goal

  • Redesign the nose cone so it is lighter and FSAE rules compliant; the previous year’s nose cone had an undersized nose radius (the minimum is 38 mm)

Approach

  • Researched mold types, materials, meshes, and weaves with a small group, and chose the best option for each
  • Learned to apply a carbon fiberglass mesh with a messy weave to a positive mold, and built the nose cone from it

Results

  • The nose cone was built and passed tech inspection
  • The car won 2nd place at the 2026 Formula Hybrid Competition
Materials and processes
Carbon fiberglass mesh laid up on a positive mold
Status
Passed tech inspection
